doc_name: Premier League Manager of the Month
text: The Premier League Manager of the Month is an award that recognises the best-performing manager each month during the Premier League season. The winner is determined by a combination of a 10% public online vote and a panel of experts. The award was previously known as the Carling Premiership Manager of the Month (1993–2001) and the Barclaycard Premiership Manager of the Month (2001–2004), and is currently called the Barclays Manager of the Month. The Premier League was established in 1992 when the First Division clubs withdrew from the Football League to form a commercially independent league that negotiated its own broadcast and sponsorship deals. The Manager of the Month award was introduced for the 1993–94 season, supplementing existing Player of the Year awards from the Football Writers' Association and Professional Footballers' Association; the first recipient was Manchester United's Alex Ferguson in August 1993. The Player of the Month award was introduced for the 1994–95 season and is presented alongside the Manager of the Month award. Ferguson holds the record with 27 Manager of the Month awards, while Harry Redknapp has won the award in five of his six spells managing Premier League clubs—West Ham United, Portsmouth, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, and Queens Park Rangers. Sixteen other managers have won the award with two or more clubs: Gordon Strachan (Coventry City, Southampton), Stuart Pearce (Nottingham Forest, Manchester City), Martin O'Neill (Leicester City, Aston Villa, Sunderland), Roy Hodgson (Blackburn Rovers, Fulham), Rafael Benítez (Liverpool, Chelsea, Newcastle United), Brendan Rodgers (Swansea City, Liverpool), Alan Pardew (West Ham United, Newcastle United), Sam Allardyce (Bolton Wanderers, West Ham United), Tony Pulis (Crystal Palace, West Bromwich Albion), Mauricio Pochettino (Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur), Claudio Ranieri (Chelsea, Leicester City), Carlo Ancelotti (Chelsea, Everton), José Mourinho (Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur), Nuno Espírito Santo (Wolverhampton Wanderers, Tottenham Hotspur, Nottingham Forest), Eddie Howe (Bournemouth, Newcastle United), and Sean Dyche (Burnley, Everton). Seventeen managers have won the award in consecutive months: Joe Kinnear, Kevin Keegan, Roy Evans, Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, David O'Leary, Stuart Pearce, Paul Jewell, Rafael Benítez, Carlo Ancelotti, Manuel Pellegrini, Claudio Ranieri, Antonio Conte, Pep Guardiola, Jürgen Klopp, Mikel Arteta, and Ange Postecoglou. Guardiola is the only manager to have won the award in four successive months, Klopp is the first to win it five times in a single season, and Postecoglou is the only manager to win it in each of his first three months in charge. The award was shared once, in March 2002, when Liverpool's Gérard Houllier and caretaker manager Phil Thompson were jointly awarded the prize due to Houllier's absence for medical reasons. As of December 2025, the most recent recipient is Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery. The award has been given monthly from the 1993–94 season through to the 2025–26 season. A table lists the number of awards won by managers with at least two wins, with managers in bold still active in the Premier League.
